Education Session - MobilityPLUS Overview
notes:
Doug Spooner, Director, Transit Services provided an education session on MobilityPLUS, which included an overview of the transit options, application process, and software for on demand service. D. Spooner shared that staff are working towards an electronic or mobile solution for fare cards, rather than using paper passes and tickets, and that staff are hoping to increase trip capacity by September 2023, by adding three more drivers. 

D. Spooner noted that the MobilityPLUS business plan will be renewed this year, and that it will important for staff to engage with customers and partner committees, in order to get a broad view of perspectives.

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, D. Spooner noted that staff are aware of the concerns with the ARBOC buses and are looking at the boarding ramp, which is not at a comfortable grade when deployed to the ground. Staff are also looking to engage partner committees on the seating layout. D. Spooner shared that staff will be revisiting the decision on ramps versus lifts as buses need to be replaced.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner explained that the purpose of the trip is not asked as per the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). D. Spooner shared that in an effort to keep capacity for on demand trips, there is a limit for subscription or pre-booked trips, and that once capacity is reached for subscription trips, there is a waiting list. 

The Committee expressed an interest to look at the application process and the opportunity to remove barriers, such as having the application be offered in different languages.

items.title: Education Session - Stage 2 ION
notes:
Matthew O'Neil, Manager, Rapid Transit Coordination provided an education session on Stage 2 ION, which included an overview of Stage 1 ION, key elements and benefits of a rapid transit system, and the work completed to date for Stage 2 ION, including a cost estimate overview. 

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes.

The Committee noted that additional information would be helpful, including a cost overview of Stage 1 ION if being built today, a map which shows the proposed LRT stops in relation to commercial and residential areas, percent of capacity filled on the trains during prime times, the possibility of starting with a BRT and converting it to a LRT later on, and the possibility of starting with LRT in Cambridge and then building the connection to Kitchener and Waterloo after.

Responding to questions from the Committee, M. O'Neil explained that the contingency costs for Stage 2 ION are in line with industry standards, and that as the risks and unknowns are reduced, the contingency will go down. M. O'Neil cautioned on starting with an LRT in Cambridge and then building the connection to Kitchener and Waterloo after, as that would result in a disconnected system, and the requirement to transfer could have a negative impact on ridership.

The Committee also stressed the importance of understanding the City of Cambridge's vision for growth, and the additional benefits of an LRT on planning and economic development.

motions.item_title: Motion to Consider Report TSD-RTS-23-001, Stage 2 ION Project Status Update
motions.text: That report TSD-RTS-23-001, Stage 2 ION Project Status Update, that was deferred to the Planning and Works Committee on June 6, 2023 be considered at this Special Planning and Works Committee meeting on May 24, 2023.
motions.text_html: That report TSD-RTS-23-001, Stage 2 ION Project Status Update, that was deferred to the Planning and Works Committee on June 6, 2023 be considered at this Special Planning and Works Committee meeting on May 24, 2023.

motions.item_title: TSD-RTS-23-001, Stage 2 ION Project Status Update
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct staff to include three project alternatives within the Stage 2 ION business case as described in report TSD-RTS-23-001 dated April 4, 2023. And that staff add to the business case: Emergency ramps; A fourth alternative be added from south terminus in Cambridge to Preston, with the construction starting in South Cambridge; and T4 where the terminus is not in the downtown Cambridge and is located in the east of Cambridge. And that staff be directed to provide information on the feasibility of adding a route down Dundas, in the City of Cambridge.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct staff to include three project alternatives within the Stage 2 ION business case as described in report TSD-RTS-23-001 dated April 4, 2023.

And that staff add to the business case:

  • Emergency ramps;
  • A fourth alternative be added from south terminus in Cambridge to Preston, with the construction starting in South Cambridge; and
  • T4 where the terminus is not in the downtown Cambridge and is located in the east of Cambridge.

And that staff be directed to provide information on the feasibility of adding a route down Dundas, in the City of Cambridge.
